extracted.intended_audience: postsecondary institution administrators, Title IX coordinators, investigators, decisionmakers, advisors, and legal counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements governing how postsecondary institutions must provide parties access to evidence (or investigative reports), protect privacy, allow review/response, and prevent unauthorized disclosures in sex-based harassment grievance procedures under §106.46.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal Opportunity To Access Evidence (§106.46(e)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: The postsecondary institution must provide each party and the party's advisor with an equal opportunity to access the evidence that is relevant to the allegations of sex-based harassment and not otherwise impermissible, consistent with §§106.2 and 106.45(b)(7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An 'equal opportunity' requires that parties have access to the same written investigative report or the underlying evidence; the institution cannot give one party access to the evidence and another party access only to an investigative report, nor provide different versions. The institution has discretion over the mode of access (electronic, physical, inspection) but must exercise that discretion to ensure parties have the same opportunity to access the material. Accommodations (auxiliary aids, language services) and extenuating circumstances may justify different modes of delivery so long as opportunity is equal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence Access Options: Underlying Evidence or Investigative Report
rubrics_metrics.description: A postsecondary institution may provide parties access to (a) the underlying relevant and not otherwise impermissible evidence or (b) access to a written investigative report that accurately summarizes that evidence. If the institution initially provides an investigative report and a party requests access to the underlying evidence, the institution must provide access to the underlying evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions may choose either option case-by-case but must articulate consistent principles in their grievance procedures for when each option will be used. Parties retain the right to request the underlying evidence even if initially provided only an investigative report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigative Report Must Be Written and Accurately Summarize Evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Unlike §106.45(f)(4) (which permits an oral description), §106.46(e)(6)(i) requires that the investigative report be a written investigative report when used as the access option.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The investigative report must accurately summarize the relevant and not otherwise impermissible evidence; providing an investigative report that fails to accurately summarize that evidence violates §106.46(e)(6)(i). Institutions commonly create written reports; they may provide both the investigative report and the underlying evidence if they choose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation on Access to Complainant's Sexual Predisposition/Prior Sexual Conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: These final regulations do not permit the parties to have any access to evidence relating to the complainant's sexual interests or prior sexual conduct unless such evidence falls within the two narrow circumstances in §106.45(b)(7)(iii): (1) offered to prove that someone other than the respondent committed the alleged conduct, or (2) concerns specific incidents of the complainant's prior sexual conduct with the respondent and is offered to prove consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a change from the 2020 amendments that had allowed broader access to 'directly related' sexual history evidence. Institutions must exclude or withhold such evidence unless it meets one of the two enumerated exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable Opportunity To Review and Respond to Evidence (§106.46(e)(6)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: A postsecondary institution must provide parties with a reasonable opportunity to review and respond to the evidence or the investigative report before determining whether sex-based harassment has occurred (and before a hearing, if one is conducted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'reasonable opportunity' standard is context-dependent: institutions must ensure parties can meaningfully review and respond given the nature and volume of evidence. Reasonableness supports prompt resolution while accommodating complex, voluminous, or sensitive files. Institutions may allow responses before, during, or after a hearing and must give additional time if the underlying evidence is later provided. §106.46(e)(5) allows extensions for good cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mode of Providing Access and Required Recordings/Transcripts
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulations do not prescribe a particular manner for sharing oral evidence or require documentary attachments to the investigative report; institutions may determine mode of access (electronic copy, physical copy, inspection). However, institutions must provide the parties with an audio or audiovisual recording or transcript of the questioning of parties and witnesses as part of the process for assessing credibility when individual meetings are held or at live hearings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although physical or electronic copies are not required, the institution must ensure meaningful access. The requirement to provide recordings/transcripts applies under §106.46(f)(1)(i)(C) (individual meetings) and §106.46(g) (live hearings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Informing Parties of Their Rights to Access (§106.46(c)(2)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Postsecondary institutions must inform parties that they are entitled to an equal opportunity to access the relevant and not otherwise impermissible evidence or an investigative report, and if the institution provides access to an investigative report, that the parties are entitled to access the relevant and not otherwise impermissible evidence upon the request of any party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This notice requirement puts parties on clear notice of their access rights and the availability of the underlying evidence upon request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance Procedures Must Articulate Consistent Principles (§106.45(b)(8))
rubrics_metrics.description: An institution's written grievance procedures must articulate consistent principles for determining whether and when it will provide access to the underlying evidence or an investigative report and for determining which procedures apply when adopting grievance procedures that apply to some, but not all, complaints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To avoid ad hoc decisions, grievance procedures could explain consideration of roles of parties, nature of conduct, severity of potential sanctions, and resource constraints when choosing the access option.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to Protect Against Unauthorized Disclosures (§106.46(e)(6)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: Postsecondary institutions must take reasonable steps to protect against parties' and their advisors' unauthorized disclosure of evidence and information obtained solely through the sex-based harassment grievance procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions should inform parties/advisors of permissible and prohibited disclosures (including disclosures authorized under §106.45(b)(5), other laws, or party consent). Reasonable steps may include policies, technical restrictions, and limited authorized disclosures. Institutions may authorize narrow disclosures to particular individuals or pieces of evidence but must balance such authorizations with privacy obligations. Institutions are not required to impose penalties for unauthorized disclosures but may do so considering circumstances. Implementation must be consistent with the First Amendment and §106.6(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and Interaction of Unauthorized Disclosure Limitation with §106.45(b)(5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section §106.46(e)(6)(iii) is narrowly framed to address privacy concerns related to information obtained solely through the grievance procedures; §106.45(b)(5) more broadly requires reasonable steps to protect parties' and witnesses' privacy during grievance procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorized disclosures under §106.46(e)(6)(iii) include disclosures permitted under §106.45(b)(5) (e.g., consulting family, confidential resources, advisors). However, disclosures of information obtained solely through procedures to friends or public posting would generally be unauthorized unless expressly allowed. Institutions must avoid authorizing widespread disclosures that would violate privacy obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Neutrality / Conflict of Interest and Bias Prohibition (§106.45(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person designated as an investigator or decisionmaker must not have a conflict of interest or bias; bias is one of the grounds for appeal under §106.46(i)(1)(iii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions must ensure investigators and decisionmakers are impartial. Allegations of conflict or bias may provide basis for appeal and OCR enforcement. This requirement interacts with the investigative report option because unfair investigation/reporting may violate §106.46(e)(6)(i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisionmaker's Use of Evidence and Written Determination (§106.46(h)(1)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: A decisionmaker cannot rely on evidence to which the parties were not given access; the written determination whether sex-based harassment occurred must include the decisionmaker's evaluation of the relevant and not otherwise impermissible evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The scope of evidence the decisionmaker must evaluate and that the parties must have an equal opportunity to access are coextensive. Failure to provide access to evidence used by the decisionmaker may violate the regulations and be subject to appeal or OCR complaint.

rubrics_metrics.name: No Requirement for Continuous Access or Dual-Format Access
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declined to require institutions to provide parties with continuous access to evidence or to require institutions to provide both the investigative report and underlying evidence at the outset; §106.46(e)(6) requires a reasonable opportunity and equal opportunity to access evidence, not continuous or duplicate access.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuous access was considered unworkable and could delay resolution. Institutions may nonetheless choose to provide both formats or continuous access, but regulation does not mandate it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals and Enforcement Related to Evidence Access (§106.46(i) and OCR enforcement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties have the right to appeal determinations based on procedural irregularity that would change the outcome, new evidence that was not reasonably available when the determination was made, and conflict of interest or bias by the Title IX Coordinator, investigator, or decisionmaker. Anyone believing a recipient has failed to comply with Title IX may file a complaint with OCR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depending on circumstances, failure to comply with §106.46(e)(6) (e.g., denial of reasonable opportunity to review, unauthorized reliance on inaccessible evidence, or improper disclosures) may be cognizable on appeal or in an OCR complaint. Institutions should consider appeals risk when implementing access procedures.
